correctness.rationale: Relative to uniform k-particle measure, the symmetric edges act on f=eta_u−eta_v by swapping occupations. A common neighbor w contributes g_w[(eta_w−eta_u)−(eta_w−eta_v)]=−g_w f, with zero swap contribution when occupations agree. On the marked bond the incoming-minus-outgoing balance of the constant and of f gives respectively (b−a)f and −(a+b)f; for equal marked occupations it gives zero. Thus the proposed affine tilt is stationary, strictly positive and normalized; connectedness gives irreducibility for 1≤k≤N−1. Summing over the two marked bits cancels the tilt for every fixed unmarked pattern. The uniform probabilities of each of 10 and 01 are P; weighting them by 1±delta and using the mean difference for symmetric-edge currents yields exactly J_uv and the triangle flows. The configuration-law terms in entropy production sum to zero by stationarity, leaving J_uv log(a/b). In the converse, if the outside means are rho, the marked deviations are d and −d. If d were zero, all symmetric currents would vanish and the driven current would be (a−b) times the strictly positive common probability of 10 and 01, contradicting stationarity. The unmarked balance at each w is then d(c_wu−c_wv)=0, proving equality of the conductances, including absent edges.
residual_risks: The proof requires connected finite graphs, intermediate fixed filling, one asymmetric bond, and a≠b for necessity. In particular a=b is an immediate counterexample to necessity if the assumption is dropped. The supplied tests concern finitely many rational instances only.

value.rationale: The structural screening criterion answers when every outside one-point observation is exactly at equilibrium despite local driving. The explicit law upgrades this to every outside joint observation at any fixed filling, even as entropy production remains strictly positive and all current is resolved on triangles. This is a useful finite-graph exception to the familiar nonlocal response to driven bonds.
residual_risks: No relaxation, fluctuation, multi-battery or infinite-volume theorem follows from this classification.
